headline: Autonomous Science Bench separates finding experimental hits from learning to rank unseen designs
summary: The authors introduce Autonomous Science Bench v0.1, an open set of six budgeted experimental campaigns grounded in published biology, chemistry and materials-science data. Its two gates separately score whether an agent discovers promising measured designs and whether its submitted model ranks unseen designs. In a pilot of eight agent-model configurations across 144 trials, the paper reports 31 full passes; Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code leads at 12 of 18, but no configuration is reliable across all campaigns. Five campaigns replay published measurements and one uses a digital twin; no physical laboratory result is reported. This is a benchmark release and author-reported pilot, not evidence that agents autonomously perform reliable real-world science.
